title: Layer-Specific Hardware Pooling Designs for CNN Accelerators
problem: CNN accelerator design typically uses uniform pooling (e.g., max pooling only), but different layers may benefit from different pooling strategies.
motivation: Optimization of hardware efficiency and model accuracy by tailoring pooling strategy to individual layers; explore combinatorial approaches beyond single pooling method.
method: Design-space exploration of combinatorial pooling techniques: combinations of Max pooling with deviation-based methods (AAD, BWAD, AMD) across different CNN layers. Evaluated on AlexNet, UNet, VGG-16. FPGA synthesis on Xilinx Zedboard; ASIC synthesis in Cadence 45nm.
key_novelty: Layer-specific pooling optimization; first systematic exploration of combinatorial pooling in CNN accelerators; demonstrates that mixed pooling strategies outperform uniform approaches.
contributions: Improved model accuracy with hardware gains
For AlexNet with pattern '110' (BWAD-BWAD-Max): 4.27% footprint saving vs Max, 14.77% vs AAD, 11.87% vs BWAD, 14.64% vs AMD
limitations: Abstract only; limited to three CNN architectures; no power consumption data; no inference latency analysis; applicability to modern architectures (ResNet, MobileNet) unclear.
